name: Solar Cold Rooms and Refrigeration
summary: Solar-powered refrigeration and cold storage units that extend the shelf life of perishable agricultural commodities, reducing post-harvest losses in off-grid locations.
description: Solar-powered cold rooms and refrigeration units use photovoltaic energy to run compressor-based refrigeration or evaporative cooling systems, enabling temperature-controlled storage of perishable products in areas without grid electricity. In Uganda's agri-energy context, solar cold rooms are deployed along agricultural value chains for dairy, fish, horticulture, and other perishable produce. Capacities range from small portable cold boxes (50–200 kg) to stand-alone insulated cold rooms (0.5 to 10 tonnes). The technology is critical for reducing post-harvest losses — estimated at 30–40% for perishables in Uganda — by extending the marketing window for farmers. Solar cold rooms are increasingly offered as pay-per-use services by agri-enterprises and cooperatives, creating sustainable business models that aggregate the produce of many smallholders.
applications: Dairy milk cooling at collection points
Fish storage at landing sites and markets
Vegetable and fruit cooling for horticulture exporters
Pharmaceutical storage in rural health facilities
Seed storage for seed enterprises and agro-dealers
benefits: Dramatically reduces post-harvest losses for perishable produce
Extends marketing window, enabling farmers to sell at better prices
Works in remote off-grid areas with no utility supply
Pay-per-use model enables shared cost recovery
Reduces food waste and improves food security
limitations: High capital cost, especially for larger units
Thermal insulation quality is critical — poor insulation undermines performance
Cooling performance depends on solar irradiance and ambient temperature
Requires trained operator and preventive maintenance
Logistics (transport to and from cold room) also need to be addressed
operationalNotes: Place cold room in a shaded, ventilated structure to reduce heat load
Pre-cool produce before placing in cold room to avoid overloading the system
Operate on a booking/scheduling system for shared facilities
Keep detailed logs of temperature readings, especially for food safety
Charge a usage fee that covers maintenance and operator costs
maintenanceNotes: Inspect refrigerant circuit and compressor every 6 months
Clean condenser coils monthly to maintain efficiency
Check door seals and insulation quarterly
Keep a spare fuse and thermostat control unit on site
